title: The Smith-Morra Gambit
description: A nasty gambit repertoire against 1.e4 c5, the Sicilian Defense. We rely on a pawn sacrifice to build a massive attack against our opponent and deliver swift checkmate.

rn2kb1r/pbq2ppp/1p1pp3/4P3/3P1P2/2PB1N2/.text: White develops the last minor piece toward the center and is now ready to castle.

rn2kb1r/pbq2ppp/1p1pp3/4P3/3P1P2/2PB4/P2.text: Black develops the light-squared bishop on the long h1-a8 diagonal and hits g2, threatening to trap the rook.

rnb1k2r/pp1p1ppp/4p3/q2nP3/1b1P4/2N5/PP1.text:
Black keeps up the pressure and renews the threat of taking on c3 and winning material.

We'll play a3, forcing Black to decide whether they are going to take on c3 or retreat the bishop.

rnb1k2r/pp1p1ppp/4p3/q2nP3/3P4/P1P5/3B1P.text:
White recaptures the bishop and creates a strong pawn chain in the center. 

Black must not be greedy and take on c3 because after 9...Nxc3, White can simply respond with 10.Qc2, when Black will lose the knight due to the pin.

rnb1k2r/pp1p1ppp/4p3/q2nP3/3P4/P1b5/1P1B.text: Black decides to trade in order to avoid having to move the bishop away and exposing their queen to unpleasant discovered attacks.

rnb1kb1r/p1q2ppp/1p1pp3/4P3/3P1P2/2P5/P2.text:
Since the light-squared bishop is blocked by e6, Black decides to open it up on the other side.

White develops the light-squared bishop and hits h7. 

This way of developing is usually very strong, especially when the opponent does not have the opportunity to develop their knight on f6.

rnb1kb1r/ppq2ppp/3pp3/4P3/3P1P2/2P5/P5PP.text:
Black develops the queen and hits the base of the pawn chain - c3.

White develops the bishop to protect the pawn and to connect the queen and the rook.

rnbqk2r/pp1p1ppp/4p3/3nP3/1b1P4/2N5/PP3P.text:
Black develops the dark-squared bishop and counters our threat by pinning the knight on c3. 

They are now threatening to win material by trading on c3.

We'll develop the dark-squared bishop and break the pin, adding more protection to c3.

rnbqkb1r/pp1p1ppp/4p3/3nP3/3P4/8/PP3PPP/.text:
Black opens up the dark-squared bishop and protects the knight on d5. 

The only downside is that it might restrict the light-squared bishop in the future.

White develops a knight and challenges the strong d5-knight at the same time. 

If Black does not react, White will trade on d5 and mess up Black's pawn structure in the center.

rnbqkb1r/pp1p1ppp/4p3/4P3/3P4/2n5/PP3PPP.text:
Black does not want to waste time on retreating so they trade instead.

White recaptures the knight and creates a strong pawn chain in the center. 

Also, the b-file is half-open now, which could be useful in the future.

rnbqkb1r/pp1ppppp/5n2/8/3pP3/2P5/PP3PPP/.text:
Black does not want to help White develop and chooses to get their knight out and hit e4 instead.

White gains more space in the center and kicks the black knight away from f6.

rnbqkb1r/pp1ppppp/8/3nP3/3p4/2P5/PP3PPP/.text:
Since Black has to move the knight away, it is usually good to place it in the center.

White regains the pawn and frees c3 for their knight.

rnbqkb1r/pp3ppp/3pp3/4P3/3P4/2P5/P4PPP/R.text:
Black immediately starts challenging White's pawn chain, since it is already deep in the enemy territory, slowing down Black's development.

White reinforces e5 at the cost of restricting their dark-squared bishop.

It is very important not to allow Black to break the pawn chain because that would leave White with multiple weaknesses.

rnbqkbnr/pp1ppppp/8/2p5/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP/R.text:
With this move, Black chooses to play the Sicilian Defense - one of the most popular responses to 1.e4. 

The idea is to trade the c- for the d-pawn and achieve an asymmetrical pawn structure. When there is asymmetry, the position is less likely to end in a draw.

We'll reply with 2.d4, a beautiful strike in the center that opens up the dark-squared bishop at the same time!

rnbqkbnr/pp1ppppp/8/8/3pP3/8/PPP2PPP/RNB.text:
Black's best option is to eliminate the d-pawn so that White does not get the opportunity to build a strong pawn center.

White plays c3, offering another pawn in exchange for better development and more piece activity, which is often more important than material in the opening phase.

rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/8/8/PPPPPPPP/RNBQK.text:
If Black plays the Sicilian Defense, they are usually looking for asymmetric and double-edged positions. 

However, in the Smith-Morra Gambit, we are going to sacrifice a pawn on c3 in order to open up the c-file and harass them for the rest of the game, making it very one-sided. In our favor, of course.

Firstly, we are going to learn how to play if our opponent declines the Gambit. Let's start with 1.e4, "Best by test." - Bobby Fischer

r1b1kb1r/pp2pppp/2n5/4P3/8/2P2N2/P4PPP/R.text:
Black brings the knight back into the game.

We'll develop the dark-squared bishop, eyeing a7, not allowing Black to be careless on the queenside.

r1b1kb1r/pp3ppp/2n1p3/4P3/8/2P1BN2/P4PPP.text:
Black opens up the dark-squared bishop at the cost of restricting the light-squared one.

We'll develop the light-squared bishop, pinning the knight on c6. 

If Black does not react, White could increase the pressure with Nd4.

r1bnkb1r/pp2pppp/8/4P3/8/2n2N2/PP3PPP/R1.text:
Black chooses to capture with the knight in order not to weaken f7.

Naturally, we recapture the knight on c3.

r1bnkb1r/pp3ppp/4p3/4P3/8/2P2N2/P4PPP/R1.text:
Black opens up the dark-squared bishop at the cost of restricting the light-squared one.

White develops the light-squared bishop and hits h7. 

Also, the bishop could at some point move to e4, from where it would not only hit h7, but also b7, hence stopping Black's queenside development.

r1bqkb1r/pp2pppp/2n5/3P4/4p3/2P2N2/P4PPP.text:
Black counter-attacks the white knight and avoids White capturing on e5 with that knight.

But we can move the knight away, getting closer to the black king.

r1bqkb1r/pp2pppp/2n5/3np3/3P4/2N2N2/PP3P.text:
Black opens up the queen in order to support d5.

White recaptures the pawn and opens up the d-file completely, hence renewing the threat of taking on d5.

r1bqkb1r/pp2pppp/2n5/4P3/8/2n2N2/PP3PPP/.text:
Black does not want to waste time on retreating the knight so they decide to trade instead.

We'll trade queens in order to either misplace the black knight or to take away the castling rights from the black king.

r1bqkb1r/pp2pppp/2n5/4p3/3P4/2P2N2/P4PPP.text:
Black breaks the pawn chain and opens up the d-file.

With d5, White declines to recapture, as that would mean agreeing to having weaknesses on c3 and e5. 

This way, White kicks the black knight away, preparing to recapture on e5 with the f3-knight.

r1bqkb1r/pp2pppp/2np4/3nP3/3P4/5N2/PP3PP.text:
Black also develops a knight and adds more pressure on d4 and e5.

We'll develop our queen's knight, challenging the strong d5-knight.

r1bqkb1r/pp2pppp/2np4/4P3/3P4/2n2N2/PP3P.text:
Black does not want to waste time on retreating the knight so they decide to trade instead.

We'll recapture, creating a strong central pawn chain.

r1bqkb1r/pp2pppp/8/3P2N1/4pB2/2Pn4/P4PPP.text:
Black has to give the pawn back, but at least they will get our light-squared bishop in exchange for that.

We capture the knight, saving our bishop on f4.

r1bqkb1r/pp2pppp/8/3P2N1/5B2/2PQ4/P4PPP/.text:
White recaptures the pawn and develops the queen at the same time. 

In the next few moves, White will castle and bring the rooks to the half-open b- and e-files and then start harassing the weak f7- and h7-pawns.

r1bqkb1r/pp2pppp/8/3P2N1/5B2/2Pp4/P4PPP/.text: Black recaptures the bishop. Otherwise, they have lost a whole piece.

r1bqkb1r/pp2pppp/8/3Pn1N1/4p3/2P5/P4PPP/.text:
Black moves the knight away from being attacked and reinforces the weak f7-pawn.

We'll develop our dark-squared bishop, harassing the loose knight in the center.

r2nk2r/pp3ppp/2b1p3/2b1P3/3N4/2PB4/P3KPP.text:
White centralizes the knight and closes the g1-a7 diagonal. We are not scared of 14...Bxg2 because of 15.Rg1, gaining the pawn back on the next move.

If Black trades on d4, it will help us reconnect our pawns and gain control of the dark squares.

r2nk2r/pp3ppp/2b1p3/2b1P3/8/2PB1N2/P3KPP.text: Black develops the dark-squared bishop and targets f2.

r2nkb1r/pp1b1ppp/4p3/4P3/8/2PB1N2/P4PPP/.text:
Black quickly develops the light-squared bishop. 

If White decides to go to e4 now, then Black will be able to challenge it with ...Bc6.

We'll play Rb1, and use the half-open b-file to harass Black's pawn.

r2nkb1r/pp3ppp/2b1p3/4P3/8/2PB1N2/P4PPP/.text:
Black moves the light-squared bishop to a better diagonal and overprotects b7.

We'll protect f3 by playing Ke2, and we will soon be ready to connect our rooks. 

When the queens are no longer on the board, it can often be safe to have the king in the center, due to there being less firepower on the board.

r3k2r/pp1bbppp/2n1p3/1B2P3/8/2P1BN2/P3KP.text:
A perfect move! 

White connects the rooks AND keeps the king close to the middle. 

White knows that now, since the queens are off the board, there is no danger of getting checkmated. 

A centralized king is often very useful as the ending approaches.

r3k2r/pp1bbppp/2n1p3/1B2P3/8/2P1BN2/P4PP.text: Black develops the dark-squared bishop and prepares to castle to connect the rooks.

r3kb1r/pp1b1ppp/2n1p3/1B2P3/8/2P1BN2/P4P.text:
Black develops the light-squared bishop, breaking the unpleasant pin.

We'll bring our rook to the open b-file, where the b7-pawn is a potential target. Our rook is well-placed to take advantage of future trades on c6, when we may be able to break into the seventh rank.

rnbq1rk1/pp3ppp/4p3/3nN3/1b1P4/2N5/PP1B1.text: Black puts their king into safety.

rnbq1rk1/pp3ppp/4p3/3nN3/1b1P4/2NB4/PP1B.text:
White develops the last minor piece and hits h7, which is weakened by the absence of a knight from f6.

In the next few moves, White will castle and then start centralizing their pieces, preparing a strong kingside attack.

rnbqk2r/pp3ppp/4p3/3nN3/1b1P4/2N5/PP3PPP.text:
Black develops the dark-squared bishop and pins the c3-knight.

We'll develop the dark-squared bishop, breaking the pin on c3.

rnbqkb1r/pp1ppppp/5n2/8/3pP3/2P5/PP3PPP/.text:
Black does not want to help White develop and chooses to get their knight out and hit e4 instead.

We'll gain more space in the center and kick the black knight away from f6.

rnbqkb1r/pp1ppppp/8/3nP3/3p4/2P5/PP3PPP/.text:
Since Black has to move the knight away, it is usually good to put it in the center.

With cxd4, White regains the pawn and frees c3 for their knight.

rnbqkb1r/pp2pppp/3p4/3nP3/3P4/8/PP3PPP/R.text:
Black immediately challenges White's pawns in order to create weaknesses for White.

We'll refuse to release the tension. Nf3 reinforces the center by developing a knight.

rnbqkb1r/pp2pppp/8/3nP3/8/5N2/PP3PPP/RNB.text:
White recaptures the pawn and fully opens the d-file. 

The e-pawn is stopping Black from ever going back to f6 with the knight, which means that White will probably develop their light-squared Bishop on d3 and later harass h7, after Black has castled kingside.

rnbqkb1r/pp2pppp/8/3np3/3P4/5N2/PP3PPP/R.text: Black releases the tension and opens up the d-file to reinforce d5.

rnbqkb1r/pp3ppp/3pp3/3nP3/3P4/5N2/PP3PPP.text:
Black opens up the dark-squared bishop and protects d5.

We'll develop our queen's knight and challenge the knight on d5.

rnbqkb1r/pp3ppp/4p3/3np3/3P4/2N2N2/PP3PP.text:
Black adds support to d5 by opening up the d-file for the queen.

We'll recapture the pawn and centralize our f3-knight. 

Now the knight is aiming at the weak-ish f7-pawn.

rnbqkbnr/pp1ppppp/8/2p5/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP/R.text:
The Sicilian! 

We reply with d4, a beautiful strike in the center that opens up the dark-squared bishop at the same time!

rnbqkbnr/pp1ppppp/8/8/3pP3/8/PPP2PPP/RNB.text:
Black's best option is to eliminate the d-pawn so that White does not get the opportunity to build a strong pawn center.

With c3, White offers another pawn in exchange for better development and more piece activity, which is often more important than material in the opening phase.

rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/8/8/PPPPPPPP/RNBQK.text:
In this study, we're going to see the Smith-Morra Declined once again. 

This time, the move that will be coupled with Nf6 will be d6.

d6 attacks the center. Let's see how we can deal with it!

We begin with 1.e4, "Best by test." - Bobby Fischer

3k1bnr/1p2pppp/r3n3/1B6/8/4BP2/PP3P1P/R3.text:
Black offers a rook for the light-squared bishop with the intention of releasing the pressure off their king.

We'll accept since the black king is still going to be exposed.

3k1bnr/4pppp/p3n3/8/8/4BP2/PP2KP1P/R6R b.text: White connects the rooks and is ready to keep harassing the black king, before Black gets the chance to develop and coordinate their pieces.

3k1bnr/4pppp/p3n3/8/8/4BP2/PP3P1P/R3K2R.text: Black has to recapture in order not to lose too much material.

3k1bnr/rp2pppp/4n3/1B6/8/5P2/PP3P1P/R1B1.text:
Black's only move.

We'll attack the rook and threaten an unpleasant check on b6.

4kbnr/rp2pppp/4n3/8/8/5P2/PP3P1P/R1B1KB1.text:
Black takes the piece, hoping to be able to develop quickly and enjoy their extra material.

We develop our bishop with check.

N4bnr/pp1kpppp/8/8/8/5P2/PP3P1P/n1BK1B1R.text:
We regain the rook. 

The black knight on a1 is trapped, whereas we can try to save ours by developing the dark-squared bishop to f4 and then getting the knight out via c7.

r1b1k1nr/pp3ppp/2n5/3q4/3Pp3/2B2N2/PP3PP.text:
Black saves the pawn by pushing it and attacking the knight on f3, also keeping the central files closed.

In reply, we centralize the knight and hit f7.

r1b1k1nr/pp3ppp/2n5/3qp3/1b1P4/2N2N2/PP3.text:
Black develops the dark-squared bishop and pins the knight on c3, hence neutralizing the attack the queen.

We'll develop our dark-squared bishop, breaking the pin on c3, and renewing the threat of capturing the queen on d5.

r1b1k1nr/pp3ppp/2n5/3qp3/3P4/2b2N2/PP1B1.text:
Black trades the knight off in order to save the queen.

We'll take back with the bishop, threatening to win the pawn on e5.

r1b1k1nr/pp3ppp/8/3qn3/3Pp3/2B5/PP3PPP/R.text:
Black decides to eliminate the strong knight.

Obviously we recapture. The d-file is now open and ready for us to use.

r1b1k2r/pp2nppp/8/3qP3/4p3/2B5/PP2BPPP/R.text:
White develops the light-squared bishop to the only safe square. We will soon castle. 

If Black refuses to trade queens, then we will move our queen to c2 and then bring a rook to the d-file.

Black will have to spend more time getting the queen out of the way.

r1b1k2r/pp2nppp/8/3qP3/4p3/2B5/PP3PPP/R2.text: Black develops the knight and protects the queen.

r1b1kbnr/pp2pppp/2n5/3q4/3P4/5N2/PP3PPP/.text: This transposes to the position we have already seen after 3...d5 in this study.

r1b1kbnr/pp2pppp/2n5/3q4/3P4/8/PP3PPP/RN.text: Black recaptures the pawn and centralizes the queen.

Black develops their knight, threatening to take on d4.

We'll develop our knight to f3, defending the pawn.

r1b1kbnr/pp3ppp/2n5/3qp3/3P4/5N2/PP3PPP/.text:
Black strikes in the center once more and opens up the dark-squared bishop.

We'll take advantage of the exposed black queen to develop our knight with a tempo.

r1bk3r/pp3ppp/2p2n2/8/1b2P3/2N2P2/PP4PP/.text: White reinforces e4 and is now ready to finish their development by getting the bishops out and then moving the king to e2 to connect the rooks.

r1bqk2r/p2p1ppp/2p2n2/8/1b2P3/2N5/PP3PPP.text:
Black recaptures toward the center and probably wants to play ...d5 in the future.

We'll develop our light-squared bishop and protect e4.

r1bqk2r/p4ppp/2p2n2/3p4/1b2P3/2NB4/PP3PP.text:
Black challenges the center and opens up their light-squared bishop.

We release the tension in order not to lose the e4-pawn.

r1bqk2r/p4ppp/2p5/3n4/1b6/2NB4/PP3PPP/R1.text: White ignores the threat on c3 and hides the king away, arguing that if Black gets greedy and goes for the pawn, their king will be punished for staying in the middle.

Black recaptures the pawn and centralizes the knight. 

They are also threatening to take on c3.

r1bqk2r/pp1p1ppp/2n2n2/8/1b1NP3/2N5/PP3P.text:
Black gets their dark-squared bishop out and pins the knight on c3, threatening to take on e4.

We'll exchange on c6 and free the d-file for our queen.

r1bqk2r/pp3ppp/2p2n2/8/1b2P3/2N5/PP3PPP/.text:
Black takes away from the center, which is normally not so good, but here, they are opening the light-squared bishop and are offering a trade of queens.

We'll accept the queen trade in order to misplace the black king. The open lines, in particular the d-file, mean that we have some prospects of causing problems.

r1bqkb1r/pp1p1ppp/2n2n2/8/3NP3/8/PP3PPP/.text:
Black develops their second knight and attacks e4.

We'll develop our queen's knight and protect e4.

r1bqkb1r/pp2pppp/2np1n2/8/4PP2/2PB1N2/PP.text:
Black develops the other knight toward the center. 

We'll simply castle.

r1bqkbnr/pp1p1ppp/2n5/4p3/3pP3/2P2N2/PP3.text:
Black develops a knight and protects the two pawns.

It is time to regain our pawn.
If Black trades everything, we will end up with a centralized queen that cannot be pushed back.

r1bqkbnr/pp1p1ppp/2n5/8/3pP3/5N2/PP3PPP/.text:
Black eliminates the d-pawn in order to destroy our  pawn center.

But we'll recapture, centralizing our knight.

r1bqkbnr/pp1ppppp/2n5/8/3pP3/2P5/PP3PPP/.text:
Black develops a knight and reinforces d4.

We'll simply regain the pawn and create a powerful pawn center.

r1bqkbnr/pp1ppppp/2n5/8/4P3/2PB4/PP3PPP/.text:
Black develops a knight toward the center.

White starts pushing their kingside pawns in order to harass the black pieces as soon as they come out. Even though White has opened up their king, Black is not developed enough to punish them.

r1bqkbnr/pp2pppp/2n5/3p4/3PP3/8/PP3PPP/R.text:
Black immediately challenges our strong center and opens up their light-squared bishop.

We'll release the tension in order to force the Queen to come out early where it can become a target for our minor pieces.

r1bqkbnr/pp2pppp/2np4/8/4PP2/2PB4/PP4PP/.text:
Black opens up the light-squared bishop and gains control of e5.

White develops a knight and prepares to castle.

r2qkb1r/pp2pppp/2np1n2/8/4PPb1/2PB1N2/PP.text:
Black develops the bishop and pins the knight on f3.

White develops a knight and reinforces f3. True, the bishop on c1 is temporarily blocked, but it will change as soon as White moves the knight either to c4 or f3.

r2qkb1r/pp3ppp/2nppn2/8/4PPb1/2PB1N2/PP1.text:
Black opens up the dark-squared bishop.

We'll develop the queen on b3, hitting b7 and delaying Black's kingside development for one more move.

r3k2r/ppq1bppp/2nppn2/8/2N1PPb1/1QPB1N2/.text: Black develops the dark-squared bishop and plans to castle on the next move.

r3k2r/ppq1bppp/2nppn2/8/4PPb1/1QPBNN2/PP.text:
White reroutes the knight toward the kingside or d5. 

In the future, White will probably try to weaken d5 by pushing f5. If the idea works, White will be able to harass the d6-pawn.

r3kb1r/ppq2ppp/2nppn2/8/4PPb1/1QPB1N2/PP.text:
Black develops the queen and protects c7. They are now ready to continue developing their minor pieces.

We'll bring our knight into the center, opening up the dark-squared bishop at the same time.

r3kbnr/pp2pppp/2n5/3q4/3P2b1/5N2/PP3PPP/.text:
Black gets the light-squared bishop out and pins the f3-knight, renewing the threat of capturing on d4.

We will develop our second knight, attacking the black queen.

r3kbnr/pp2pppp/2n5/3q4/3P4/2N2b2/PP3PPP/.text:
Black eliminates one of the defenders of d4, hoping to win free material.

We recapture with the pawn, not allowing Black to exchange queens on f3. We have a clever idea in mind.

r3kbnr/pp2pppp/2n5/8/3q4/2N2P2/PP3P1P/R1.text:
Black takes the pawn, but ignores their development.

White trades the queens in order to eliminate one of the few active black pieces.

r3kbnr/pp2pppp/4n3/1N6/8/5P2/PP3P1P/R1B1.text:
Black moves the knight back to guard c7.

Now we capture on a7, a clever sacrifice to take advantage of the fact that Black's kingside is still asleep.

r3kbnr/pp2pppp/8/1N6/8/5P2/PP3P1P/n1BK1B.text:
Black has no choice, but to take the rook. Otherwise, they lose either their knight or the rook.

Now it is time for us to gain our material back with interest!

r3kbnr/pp2pppp/8/1N6/8/5P2/PPn2P1P/R1B1K.text:
Black is going all in.

White moves the king out of check without blocking any of the bishops and attacks the knight.

r3kbnr/pp2pppp/8/8/3n4/2N2P2/PP3P1P/R1B1.text:
Black has to recapture the queen. 

Now we play Nb5. This is our big idea. We ignore the fork on c2 and make our own threats, arguing that our better development should decide the tactical battle to our advantage.

r4bnr/ppNkpppp/8/8/8/5P2/PP3P1P/n1BK1B1R.text: Black moves the king out of check and attacks the knight.

rnb1kbnr/pp2pppp/8/3q4/3p4/2P5/PP3PPP/RN.text:
Black recaptures the pawn and centralizes the queen, also hitting g2, stopping our bishop from coming out.

We'll capture the pawn, opening c3 for our knight.

rnbqkbnr/pp1p1ppp/8/4p3/3pP3/2P5/PP3PPP/.text:
Black declines our sacrifice and reinforces d4, opening up the dark-squared bishop at the same time.

We'll develop our knight towards the center and immediately attack d4 and e5.

rnbqkbnr/pp1ppppp/8/2p5/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP/R.text:
The Sicilian! 

We'll strike in the center with d4, opening up the dark-squared bishop at the same time!

rnbqkbnr/pp1ppppp/8/8/3pP3/8/PPP2PPP/RNB.text:
Black's best option is to eliminate the d-pawn so that White does not get the opportunity to build a strong pawn center.

With c3, we offer another pawn in exchange for better development and more piece activity, which is often more important than material in the opening phase.

rnbqkbnr/pp1ppppp/8/8/4P3/2Pp4/PP3PPP/RN.text:
Black refuses to take on c3 and also does not want White to capture on d4. Therefore, they choose to give the pawn back on d3 and keep the position as closed as possible.

We'll take the pawn and develop the light-squared bishop.

rnbqkbnr/pp2pppp/8/3p4/3pP3/2P5/PP3PPP/R.text:
Black refuses to accept our pawn sacrifice and immediately strikes in the center, opening up their light-squared bishop at the same time.

We'll capture on d5, and induce the black queen to come out where we can target her.

rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/8/8/PPPPPPPP/RNBQK.text:
Black could deviate from the gambit in a myriad of ways.

Some of these deviations aren't particularly good: 3...e5, supporting the pawn on d4, simply allows us to take on d4, for example. 

Then there's 3...d3, pushing the pawn forward to make us recapture and keep a pawn on c3 (where our knight should have been). 

And there's other moves like 3...Nc6 or d5, which we'll explore and find a strategy against. Let's being, starting with 1.e4!

1rbqkb1r/3p2pp/p1n1ppn1/1p1N4/4P3/1B2BN2.text: Black refuses to take the knight in order to avoid giving White too much activity and also stops the white bishop from coming to b6.

We put the rook on the same file as the black king in case Black ever decides to capture on d5. 

Black is in a lot of trouble because it is very hard for them to find good developing moves.

r1bq1rk1/pp1pppbp/2n3pn/4P3/2B2B2/2N2N2/.text:
White develops the dark-squared bishop and protects e5.

In the next few moves, White will most likely connect the rooks and then start exerting pressure on the d7-pawn, not allowing Black to ever develop their light-squared bishop and coordinate their rooks.

r1bq1rk1/pp1pppbp/2n3pn/4P3/2B5/2N2N2/PP.text: Black puts the king into safety.

r1bq2nr/pp1pp1kp/6p1/3Qb3/8/2N5/PP3PPP/R.text:
Black tries to keep the king safe. Kf6 would be too risky.

We'll simply regain our piece with Qxe5+.

r1bq2nr/pp1ppk1p/6p1/4b3/8/2N5/PP3PPP/R1.text:
Black eliminates the strong light-squared bishop.

Our queen will arrive on d5, forking the king and the bishop.

r1bq3r/pp1pp1kp/5np1/4Q3/8/2N5/PP3PPP/R1.text: Black blocks the check and develops the knight.

We'll castle into safety.

Soon enough, we will finish our development and then start harassing the pawns on the d- and e-files. The dark squares around the black king are also weak.

r1bqk1nr/pp1ppp1p/6p1/4b3/2B5/2N5/PP3PPP.text:
Black has to recapture. Otherwise, they have lost a piece.

Now we hit Black with Bf7, temporarily sacrificing the bishop in order to lure the black king out to set up a fork.

r1bqk1nr/pp1pppbp/2n3p1/8/2B1P3/2N2N2/PP.text:
Black develops the dark-squared bishop and eyes c3.

With e5, we block the long diagonal and gains more space in the center. Even though it looks like the e-pawn is free for Black to take, White can win it back with a tactic.

r1bqk1nr/pp1pppbp/6p1/4n3/2B5/2N2N2/PP3P.text:
Black is greedy and grabs the central pawn.

We'll trade knights in order to lure the dark-squared bishop out into the open.

r1bqk2r/pp1pppbp/2n3pn/4P3/2B5/2N2N2/PP3.text:
Black develops the knight and intends to castle as soon as possible. 

The knight seems offside at the moment, but it will most likely get back into play via f5.

We'll simply castle.

r1bqkb1r/1p1p2pp/p1n1ppn1/8/2B1P3/2N1BN2.text:
Black gets the knight out of the bishop's way. They need to castle before pushing any pawns in the center.

We retreat the bishop back to b3 so that ...Ne5 or ...b5 does not come with a tempo.

r1bqkb1r/1p1pn1pp/p1n1pp2/6B1/2B1P3/2N2N.text:
Black breaks the pin and attacks the white bishop. However, they have now weakened their king.

We pull the bishop back and eye the soft spot on b6.

r1bqkb1r/1p1pnppp/p1n1p3/8/2B1P3/2N2N2/P.text:
Black develops a knight and plans to push ...d5 if White allows it.

With Bg5, we develop the dark-squared bishop and indirectly stop Black from pushing ...d5 by pinning the knight on e7 to the queen.

r1bqkb1r/3p2pp/p1n1ppn1/1p6/4P3/1BN1BN2/.text:
Black gains space on the queenside and opens up the light-squared bishop.

In reply, we will play a thematic piece sacrifice, taking advantage of Black's undeveloped kingside. 

The threat is Bb6, trapping the black queen.

r1bqkb1r/3p2pp/p1n2pn1/1p1p4/4P3/1B2BN2/.text:
Black accepts the sacrifice, hoping to be able to develop quickly and enjoy their extra material.

We'll capture the pawn and kick the black knight from c6.

r1bqkb1r/3p2pp/p4pn1/1p1Pn3/8/1B2BN2/PP3.text:
Black decides to centralize the knight and hopes to trade a few pieces to reduce the pressure and coordinate their pieces more easily.

With d6, we gains even more space and cut the black position in two. The concrete threat is Qd5, forking the rook and f7.

r1bqkbnr/1p1p1ppp/p1n1p3/8/2B1P3/2N2N2/P.text:
Black stops the white knight from ever getting to b5, from where it could harass the d6-square, and prepares to push ...b5 at some point.

We'll castle, continuing our rapid development.

r1bqkbnr/1p3ppp/p1npp3/8/2B1P3/2N2N2/PP2.text: White moves the queen off the d-file in order to be able to put the rook from f1 on d1. White will soon finish their development and then try to achieve the e5-breakthrough.

r1bqkbnr/1p3ppp/p1npp3/8/2B1P3/2N2N2/PP3.text: Black opens up the light-squared bishop and plugs the hole on d6.

r1bqkbnr/pp1p1ppp/2n1p3/8/4P3/2N2N2/PP3P.text:
Black opens up the light-squared bishop and prepares to push ...d5 at some point.

We'll develop our the light-squared bishop and stop Black from breaking free with ...d5.

r1bqkbnr/pp1ppp1p/2n3p1/8/4P3/2N2N2/PP3P.text:
Black decides to open up the dark-squared bishop and put it on the long a1-h8 diagonal, from where it will exert indirect pressure on the center by eyeing the c3-knight.

We'll develop the light-squared bishop and hit f7.

r1bqkbnr/pp1ppppp/2n5/8/4P3/2N5/PP3PPP/R.text:
Black develops a knight towards the center and gains control over e5.

We'll develop our second knight and take over control of e5.

r1bqkbnr/pp3ppp/2npp3/8/2B1P3/2N2N2/PP2Q.text: White moves the queen off the d-file so that a rook can occupy d1 in the future.

r1bqkbnr/pp3ppp/2npp3/8/2B1P3/2N2N2/PP3P.text: Black opens up the light-squared Bishop and plugs the hole on d6.

r2qkb1r/1b1p2pp/p2P1pn1/1p2n3/8/1B2BN2/P.text:
Black develops the light-squared bishop and stops the white queen from getting to d5.

We'll trade knights on e5 in order to open up the way for the f-pawn.

r2qkb1r/1b1p2pp/p2P2n1/1p2p3/5P2/1B2B3/P.text: We open up the central files in order to punish Black for being greedy and taking material instead of developing and getting their king into safety. In practice, this position is difficult to play for Black.

r2qkb1r/1b1p2pp/p2P2n1/1p2p3/8/1B2B3/PP3.text: Black recaptures the piece and tries to keep the e-file closed.

rnbqkbnr/pp1ppppp/8/2p5/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP/R.text:
The Sicilian Defense!

With d4, we strike in the center and open up our dark-squared bishop at the same time!

rnbqkbnr/pp1ppppp/8/8/3pP3/8/PPP2PPP/RNB.text:
Black's best option is to eliminate the d-pawn so that White does not get the opportunity to build a strong pawn center.

With c3, we offer another pawn in exchange for better development and more piece activity, which is often more important than material in the opening phase.

rnbqkbnr/pp1ppppp/8/8/4P3/2p5/PP3PPP/RNB.text:
Black wins a pawn, but helps White get quicker development.

We'll recapture the pawn and develop a knight.

rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/8/8/PPPPPPPP/RNBQK.text:
In this chapter, we will keep learning about the Smith-Morra Gambit, in which White offers a pawn in exchange for the open c-file and better development.

In this part of the course, we will have a look at how to treat positions where Black accepts our pawn and keeps it. We'll begin with 1.e4. "Best by test." - Bobby Fischer

r1b1k2r/1pq1bppp/p1nppn2/8/2B1PB2/2N2N2/.text:
White brings the other rook into play and puts it on the same file as the black queen, creating an unpleasant x-ray on the c-file. 

White has now fully developed and Black still needs to find a good way of coordinating their pieces without losing material in the process.
Black develops the dark-squared bishop and gets ready to castle.

r1b1kb1r/1pq2ppp/p1nppn2/8/2B1P3/2N2N2/P.text:
Black develops their second knight and gets one step closer to castling.

We will develops our dark-squared bishop and place further pressure on d6.

r1b1kb1r/1pq2ppp/p2ppn2/4n3/2B1PB2/2N2N2.text:
Black blocks the diagonal and accepts the possibility of having doubled e-pawns.

We will trade our bishop for the knight, removing the only active black piece and doubling Black's pawns.

r1b1kb1r/1pq2ppp/p3pn2/4p3/2B1P3/2N2N2/P.text:
We will bring our other rook into play, placing it on the same file as the black queen, creating an unpleasant x-ray.

Black will have to spend more time on solving that problem, which will further delay their development.

r1b1kbnr/1pq2ppp/p1npp3/8/2B1P3/2N2N2/PP.text:
Black moves their queen away from the d-file, knowing that the white rook will soon arrive there.

We will play Rd1, and exert pressure on d6.

r1bQ1b1r/pp2pkpp/5n2/4p3/8/2N5/PP3PPP/R1.text: But now we can just take the queen, with a completely winning position.

r1bk1b1r/pp2pppp/2n2n2/4p1N1/2B5/2N5/PP3.text: We attack with the knight, threatening a nasty fork on f7. It is not clear how Black can avoid losing material.

r1bk1b1r/pp2pppp/2n2n2/4p3/2B5/2N2N2/PP3.text:
Black captures with the king in order to keep protecting e5. 

However, f7 is now weak.

r1bnkb1r/pp2pppp/5n2/1N2p3/2B5/5N2/PP3PP.text:
We attack with the knight and threaten a nasty fork on c7.

It is not clear how Black will counter this threat without making huge concessions.

r1bnkb1r/pp2pppp/5n2/4p3/2B5/2N2N2/PP3PP.text: Black decides to give the pawn back and try to keep the king safe.

r1bq1rk1/pp2bppp/2np1n2/4p3/2B1P3/2N1BN2.text:
We play Rc1, bringing the other rook into play and finishing our development.

r1bqk2r/pp2bppp/2np1n2/4p3/2B1P3/2N2N2/P.text:
Black blocks White's push and opens up the light-squared bishop. 

However, they have created a big hole on d5 and our knight will be more than happy to jump in there in the future.

We'll develop our dark-squared bishop, connecting our rooks.

r1bqk2r/pp2bppp/2nppn2/8/2B1P3/2N2N2/PP2.text:
Black develops the dark-squared bishop and gets ready to castle.

We'll bring our rook to the same file as the black queen and pin the d-pawn, threatening to play e5.

r1bqkb1r/pp2p1pp/2n1p3/3pn1N1/5B2/1BN5/P.text: White develops the dark-squared bishop and puts pressure on e5. The threat is Qe2, forcing the knight to move away and then capturing e6. Black also has problems completing their development.

r1bqkb1r/pp2p1pp/2n1p3/3pn1N1/8/1BN5/PP3.text: Black blocks the diagonal and saves the pawn.

r1bqkb1r/pp2p1pp/2npp3/4n1N1/2B5/2N5/PP3.text:
Black pulls the knight back and hits the white bishop.

We'll retreat our bishop and continue to threaten to capture on e6.

r1bqkb1r/pp2p1pp/2npp3/8/2B3n1/2N2N2/PP3.text:
Black wins a pawn, but opens up the king.

Now we carry on the attack with Ng5. Both the pawn on e6 and the knight on g4 are under attack.

r1bqkb1r/pp2pppp/2n2n2/4p3/2B5/2N2N2/PP3.text:
Black takes the pawn in order to save the f6-knight from having to move away.

We'll trade the queens in order to either misplace the enemy king and weaken f7, or to misplace the black knight and regain the pawn.

r1bqkb1r/pp2pppp/2np1n2/8/2B1P3/2N2N2/PP.text:
Black develops their second knight, hitting e4.

In response, we'll push forward with e5, opening the central files immediately.

r1bqkb1r/pp2pppp/2np4/4P3/2B3n1/2N2N2/PP.text:
Black refuses to open up the d-file and moves the knight forward, hitting e5.

We will sacrifice the e-pawn in order to disrupt the coordination between Black's pieces.

r1bqkb1r/pp2pppp/3p1n2/4n3/2B5/2N2N2/PP3.text:
Black grabs the pawn and centralizes the knight. It would be a nice move, if White could not win material immediately.

We'll capture the knight in order to open up the d-file.

r1bqkb1r/pp2pppp/5n2/4p3/2B5/2N5/PP3PPP/.text:
Black recaptures the piece and hopes to develop quickly. 

However, their king is now overloaded with defending both d8 and f7...

And we'll strike with Bxf7+!

r1bqkb1r/pp3ppp/2nppn2/8/2B1P3/2N2N2/PP2.text:
Black develops the second knight toward the center and is one step closer to castling.

We'll castle, getting our king into safety.

r1bqkbnr/1p3ppp/p1npp3/8/2B1P3/2N2N2/PP2.text:
Black takes away the possibility of Nb5 from White and prepares to gain space on the queenside with ...b5.

We'll simply castle.

r1bqkbnr/pp1ppppp/2n5/8/4P3/2N5/PP3PPP/R.text:
Black develops a knight towards the center and gains control over e5.

We'll develop our second knight and take control of e5.

r1bqkbnr/pp2pppp/2np4/8/4P3/2N2N2/PP3PPP.text:
Black opens up the light-squared bishop.

We will develop our light-squared bishop, hitting f7.

r1bqkbnr/pp3ppp/2npp3/8/2B1P3/2N2N2/PP3P.text:
Black blocks the white bishop and opens up e7 for their dark-squared bishop.

We'll move our queen off the d-file so that one of the rooks can occupy d1 in the future, exerting pressure on d6 and preparing the e5-push.

r2q1bnr/pp2pkpp/2np4/6N1/4P1b1/2N5/PP3PP.text:
White checks the black king and discovers an attack on the loose g4-bishop. 

White will regain the piece on the next move and then harass the black king, which has lost castling rights.

r2q1bnr/pp2pkpp/2np4/8/4P1b1/2N2N2/PP3PP.text: Black eliminates the strong white bishop.

r2qkb1r/pp2p1pp/2npp3/8/6n1/2N2N2/PP3PPP.text:
Black has to recapture.

We'll activate the knight and threaten to take on g4 and e6.

r2qkb1r/pp2p1pp/2nppn2/6N1/8/2N5/PP3PPP/.text:
Black retreats the knight to safety.

We'll regain a pawn and attack the black queen.

r2qkb1r/pp2pppp/2npb3/8/2B3n1/2N2N2/PP3P.text:
Black captures the pawn and forces a trade of bishops.

We'll simply exchange on e6, leaving Black with weaknesses around their king.

r2qkbnr/pp2pppp/2np4/8/2B1P1b1/2N2N2/PP3.text:
Black develops the light-squared bishop and pins the knight on f3. 

However, the bishop is undefended and White can immediately punish it with Bxf7+! This temporarily sacrifices the bishop in order to lure the black king out.

r3kb1r/pp1qp1pp/2npNn2/8/8/2N5/PP2QPPP/R.text:
White adds support to the e6-knight, not allowing Black to develop properly. 

White will soon castle, finish their development and then start harassing the black king, which is stuck in the center.

r3kb1r/pp1qp1pp/2npNn2/8/8/2N5/PP3PPP/R1.text: Black moves the queen and attacks the white knight, hoping to kick it out of e6 and then push the e-pawn.

rnbqkbnr/pp1ppppp/8/2p5/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP/R.text:
The Sicilian.

With d4, we strike in the center and open up the dark-squared bishop!

rn1qkb1r/1b3ppp/p2p1n2/3P4/1p1Q4/1B3N2/P.text:
Black develops a knight and blocks the line of attack on g7.

We'll capture another pawn and target the b7-bishop.

rn1qkbnr/1b1p1ppp/p3p3/1p6/4P3/1BN2N2/PP.text:
Black develops the bishop and adds more control over d5.

rn1qkbnr/1b1p1ppp/p3p3/8/1p2P3/1BN2N2/PP.text:
Black kicks the knight from c3 and hopes to be able to play ...d5 next.

rn1qkbnr/1b1p1ppp/p7/3p4/1p2P3/1B3N2/PP3.text:
Black takes a piece and intends to develop quickly to capitalize on their extra material.

We'll capture the pawn and open up the e-file.

rn1qkbnr/1b3ppp/p2p4/3P4/1p6/1B3N2/PP3PP.text:
Black blocks the white d-pawn to stop it from gaining more space and slowing down Black's development even more.

rnbq1rk1/pp2bppp/3ppn2/8/2B1P3/2N2N2/PP2.text: Black gets their king into safety.

rnbqk1nr/pp1p1pbp/4p1p1/1N6/2B1P3/1Q6/PP.text: We activate the knight and threaten to jump into d6, displacing the black king. The dark squares around the black king are a serious weakness.

rnbqk1nr/pp1p1pbp/4p1p1/8/2B1P3/1QN5/PP3.text: Black blocks the diagonal to stop the threat against f7.

rnbqk1nr/pp1pppbp/6p1/8/2B1P3/2N5/PP3PPP.text:
Black develops the dark-squared bishop on the long diagonal and takes aim at c3.

We'll develop the queen and attack f7.

rnbqk1nr/pp2bppp/3pp3/8/2B1P3/2N2N2/PP3P.text:
Black develops the dark-squared bishop and is one step closer to castling.

We'll castle our king into safety.

rnbqk2r/pp2bppp/3ppn2/8/2B1P3/2N2N2/PP3P.text:
Black develops a knight and gets ready to castle.

We'll develop the queen and free d1 for one of the rooks.

rnbqkbnr/1p1p1ppp/p3p3/8/2B1P3/2N5/PP3PP.text:
Black prepares to push ...b5 and open up their light-squared bishop which is currently very restricted.

Black attacks our bishop and opens up their light-squared bishop at the same time.

rnbqkbnr/pp1p1ppp/4p3/8/4P3/2N5/PP3PPP/R.text:
Black opens up the dark-squared bishop and intends to play the freeing ...d5.

rnbqkbnr/pp1ppp1p/6p1/8/4P3/2N5/PP3PPP/R.text:
Black decides to fianchetto the dark-squared bishop.

Black opens up the light-squared bishop.

In this study, we'll see some ways Black may have of trying to hold on to the pawn.

Spoiler alert: these methods are bad!
